item.title: Why New York turned 5,000 discarded toilets into oyster reefs beneath Jamaica Bay
item.description: New York City repurposed nearly five thousand old toilets into artificial reef structures. These porcelain fixtures now provide a base for juvenile oyster growth in Jamaica Bay. Oyster reefs are vital for filtering pollutants and improving water quality in New York Harbour. Decades of pollution and overfishing had previously destroyed these important natural systems. This initiative supports broader coastal resilience and habitat restoration efforts across the region.

item.title: Quote of the day by Emma Watson: ‘Don't let anyone tell you what you can and can't do,’ and why limits are often imposed before they are real
item.description: Emma Watson's post-Harry Potter journey is a testament to breaking barriers and redefining success. Opting for higher education and championing gender equality over conventional Hollywood roles, she embodies the spirit of the saying, 'Don't let anyone tell you what you can and can't do.' Watson's story motivates others to carve out their own paths and pursue their goals with unwavering conviction.
item.dc:creator: TOI News Desk

item.title: Meet ‘Granny H’, the mystery knitter leaving toys for children
item.description: A ninety-year-old woman named June Rose Hood secretly left knitted toys for village children. These mysterious gifts appeared for two years, sparking much speculation among residents. Hood, known as Granny H, found knitting therapeutic and a way to manage anxiety. Her grandson helped hide the handmade toys, which brought smiles to many faces. The community later celebrated Hood's kindness and her significant contribution to their village.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US dumped 2 million tyres in the 1970s to help marine life; cleanup continues
item.description: Millions of old vehicle tyres were placed offshore near Broward County for artificial reefs. Shifting currents and storms scattered these tyres, damaging existing coral reefs. Government agencies are now undertaking a massive, multi-year cleanup operation. Specialist divers and equipment are required for this extensive recovery effort. This project highlights the long-term consequences of environmental initiatives.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Scientists reveal how green roofs cut rooftop temperatures by 40°F
item.description: Green roofs offer a solution to urban heat by absorbing sunlight and releasing water. Vegetation shades surfaces and evapotranspiration naturally cools surrounding areas. These living roofs also manage rainwater and provide habitats for urban wildlife. Extensive and intensive systems cater to different building needs and budgets. Cities worldwide are adopting green roofs to combat rising temperatures and improve environments.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Why were Naruto and Safine handed suspended sentences over Jean Pormanove? Here’s what we know
item.description: Owen Cenazandotti and Safine Hamadi, two French streamers, received suspended sentences for their actions during streamed content. The court has prohibited them from uploading any online material for six months. Their content, aired from 2023 to 2025, showcased disturbing violence against people. Despite calls for stricter consequences, their sentences remain on hold unless they breach conditions set by the court.

item.title: US buried 56 million gallons of highly radioactive waste during Cold War, now experts will use it to make 4.2 metric tons of glass daily
item.description: During the Cold War, the Hanford Site was vital to the U.S. nuclear program, generating plutonium but also creating a daunting legacy of hazardous radioactive waste—millions of gallons of it. Vitrification is at the heart of the solution, as it transforms this hazardous material into glass for safer long-term storage. The Vit Plant has started processing actual nuclear waste and aims for consistent glass production.

item.title: As Japan battles a 'cruelly hot' summer, lions and people are falling victim to the heatwave at a record pace
item.description: Amidst deadly heat waves, Japan faces a growing crisis marked by significant hospitalizations and loss of life. These soaring temperatures are thwarting recovery initiatives in earthquake-impacted areas. In a heartbreaking occurrence, three lions at a Tokyo zoo succumbed to the heat. In response, officials have issued a heatstroke warning for vast regions of western and southern Japan, introducing the term 'kokushobi' to highlight these dangerously hot days.

"I just got violated": Twitch streamer Austin McBroom reacts after woman grabs him on livestream
item.description: Twitch streamer Austin McBroom reacted with shock after a woman appeared to grab him during a livestream. He stated he felt violated, questioning the laughter of onlookers at the moment. This incident has prompted widespread discussion about the importance of consent and unwanted touching. Some viewers question if the livestream event was genuinely unplanned or staged for attention.

item.title: White phosphorus scare: US military denies chemical leak at South Korea military base
item.description: In a precautionary measure, South Korean officials advised residents to evacuate Osan Air Base following reports of a potential white phosphorus leak. The US military promptly investigated and concluded that there was no trace of the hazardous material. Subsequent analysis identified the residue as harmless corrosion from environmental factors. The evacuation notice was rescinded after successful decontamination efforts, with no injuries reported at the site.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: Chicago study links more urban tree cover to fewer deaths
item.description: A new study by Northwestern University has found that neighbourhoods in Chicago that lost more tree canopy over 11 years also recorded higher mortality rates, particularly in hotter areas. The researchers say protecting mature trees, along with planting new ones, could help reduce heat-related health risks and improve public health in cities.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Scientists turn factory exhaust carbon dioxide into useful chemicals, study reveals
item.description: A team of scientists has pioneered an advanced system that converts carbon dioxide directly from factory emissions. This groundbreaking process sidesteps expensive gas separation and purification techniques. By utilizing specially formulated organic electrolytes, the system successfully facilitates the conversion of CO2 into carbon monoxide while minimizing unwanted reactions. This innovation presents a cost-effective solution for curbing carbon emissions from industries.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Chubby marmots join subscription service after sanctuary faces money trouble
item.description: In a creative twist, a biologist from Colorado turned to popular subscription service to secure funding for crucial marmot research. He shares engaging and family-oriented videos featuring yellow-bellied marmots, motivated by recent federal budget cuts affecting his long-standing project. Operating for over sixty years, this initiative not only raises awareness about marmot populations but has also begun to generate essential financial support for ongoing scientific investigations.
